item.title: APEC growth forecast upgraded to 3.4 percent
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
The economy of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation region is projected to grow 3.4 percent in 2026, supported by strong technology investments even as energy costs and trade restrictions weigh on the outlook. "We have a combination of upside opportunities but also downside risks," said Carlos Kuriyama, director of the APEC Policy Support Unit. Speaking at an online media briefing held on Sunday by the APEC Secretariat ahead of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, which will be held on Wednesday and Thursday in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, Kuriyama said that regional economic growth has remained resilient, but the economic environment is becoming more challenging. The latest growth forecast is higher than the earlier projection of 3.2 percent, according to the report released by the APEC Policy Support Unit on Sunday. Trade in goods has provided a significant boost. In the first half of 2026, the export values of all APEC member economies combined surged 22.5 percent year-on-year, compared with 6.5 percent a year earlier. While the trade outlook for this year is relatively good, Kuriyama said that he expects a moderation in the growth of export and import volume over the next two years, due to economic challenges, supply chain restrictions and trade policy uncertainty. Inflation is also expected to increase to 3.2 percent in 2026, up 0.8 percentage point from 2025, driven by higher energy prices and electricity costs. "Based on the current situation, we are advocating … for policy priorities," said Kuriyama, stressing the need for an effective mix of monetary and fiscal policy, diversifying investments and energy sources, strengthening the trade environment and fortifying multilateral links. Also at the media briefing, Eduardo Pedrosa, executive director of the APEC Secretariat, said that building resilience is a key focus of this year's APEC discussions. Under China's rotating chairmanship, APEC has set openness, innovation and cooperation as priorities. Pedrosa noted that APEC economies represent more than 60 percent of global GDP, and that roughly 300 meetings have been held this year, including a trade ministers' meeting in May in Suzhou, Jiangsu province. "I think what makes APEC unique is that we are a process," said Pedrosa, adding that APEC provides a platform for regional economic leaders and the business community, enabling member economies to engage. kelly@chinadailyapac.com

item.title: Shenzhen ready to welcome Asia-Pacific leaders
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
At the APEC media center in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on Saturday, Russia Today journalist Mariia Cherdantseva watched a robot prepare coffee — a sight that she had expected in a city often dubbed "China's Silicon Valley". Having previously visited Shenzhen, Cherdantseva said that she is impressed every time by how the city has developed. She found the center's artificial intelligence applications both useful for journalists and fun to interact with. The media center, which opened on Nov 11 for journalists covering the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Week, offers a glimpse into the city's preparations for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting on Wednesday and Thursday. Shenzhen will become the third Chinese city to host the event, after Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. This year's meeting is themed "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together", with openness, innovation and cooperation as priorities. The city's preparations extend well beyond the media center, bringing together conference arrangements, visitor services and technology to welcome guests from across the Asia-Pacific. At a news briefing on Saturday, Shenzhen Mayor Li Yun said that all of the meeting venues were ready following equipment checks and full rehearsals. Dedicated channels for delegates have been established at nine ports of entry spanning sea, land, air and rail routes. Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport has introduced advanced screening technology for checked baggage in order to streamline clearance, Li said. More than 100,000 foreign-language signs have been standardized across the city, and over 7,000 AI translation devices have been installed at transport hubs, tourist attractions and shopping areas. Visitors can use bank cards issued overseas to pay for metro rides or withdraw cash from more than 3,000 ATMs across the city, while 1,360 conference volunteers and tens of thousands of city volunteers are on hand to help. The use of technology in the preparations reflects Shenzhen's broader strengths in innovation and manufacturing. Xia Lei, deputy director of the city's science and technology innovation bureau, said that Shenzhen's industry has long generated more than 30 percent of its GDP, helping to translate research findings in laboratories into market-ready products. He pointed to the Huaqiangbei electronics market and the city's extensive supply chains as part of the ecosystem in which technology businesses have grown. Shenzhen has given rise to global technology leaders including Huawei, BYD, Tencent and DJI. The city posted GDP of 3.87 trillion yuan ($580 billion) in 2025, with research and development spending reaching 7.1 percent of GDP — the highest ratio among Chinese cities for the second consecutive year. That industrial strength is underpinned by an extensive network of regional trade and investment. During the first nine months of 2026, trade with other APEC economies rose 40 percent year-on-year, accounting for nearly 70 percent of Shenzhen's total foreign trade. Shenzhen companies invested $4.1 billion in those economies, accounting for more than 60 percent of the city's outward investment volume, according to data-released at Saturday's briefing. The city has also become the first on the Chinese mainland to surpass 5 trillion yuan in foreign trade, with imports and exports reaching 5.25 trillion yuan in the first 10 months of 2026, according to customs data. Zhang Feimeng, director-general of Shenzhen's commerce bureau, said that imports reached 2.24 trillion yuan in the first three quarters, up 70.1 percent, as the city worked to open its market wider to overseas suppliers. Meanwhile, Shenzhen's combined exports of competitive products, such as 3D printers, digital cameras and smartphones, grew 15.5 percent during the same period. Ma Jiangtao, founding director of the Doctorate Association — a nonprofit organization based in the United Kingdom that connects global scholars for academic exchanges — said that a city's international character is built through genuine exchanges and tangible business opportunities. He expressed hope that continued opening-up would attract more international visitors to China, unlocking more opportunities for cooperation. Du Lan, deputy director of the China Institute of International Studies' Department for Asia-Pacific Studies, said that Shenzhen's use of technology and city services to welcome international guests signals a broader opportunity for China to support Asia-Pacific growth through market openness and innovation cooperation. China can leverage its vast market to offer businesses more predictable market access by promoting trade and investment liberalization and closer alignment with regional trade arrangements, Du said. item.title: Why does skyscraper-studded Shenzhen draw migratory birds year after year?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
Every autumn and winter, large numbers of migratory birds arrive in Shenzhen, either to rest over the winter or pass through on their journeys. What makes this modern metropolis such a reliable, welcoming stop for these avian travelers returning like clockwork each year? China Daily reporter Yan An ventured into the mangrove forests of Shenzhen Bay with Zhang Gaofeng, secretary-general of the Shenzhen Bird Watching Society, to find the answer. During the 2026 APEC "China Year", China and Asia-Pacific economies continue to deepen green cooperation, jointly address ecological and environmental challenges and safeguard regional ecological security and biodiversity. The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will take place in Shenzhen from Nov 18 to 19. Stay tuned to see how this gathering will advance more cooperation across the Asia-Pacific region.

item.title: Striding in Sync
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
Growing up in Sydney and now building a career in Shenzhen, Laurie Pearcey's life is the story of a cross-border bond forged across ocean expanses. In Sydney he met his Chinese wife; in Shenzhen he has embraced the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and all it has to offer. Beyond personal ties, deep-rooted links in education, trade and technology — from laser innovation to drone applications — unite people and industries in both cities. With Shenzhen hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, this mutual engagement highlights openness, innovation and cooperation — the three priorities of the 2026 APEC "China Year". APEC was established in Australia in 1989, since when member economies have striven to improve the prosperity of their peoples.

item.title: Why Asia-Pacific needs common prosperity? Insights from a former Cambodian minister
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
In a recent interview with China Daily's Global Lens, Pou Sothirak, Cambodia's former minister of industry, mines and energy, said that the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting offers an important opportunity for regional economies to deepen cooperation and share development opportunities. Although Cambodia is not an APEC member, Sothirak expressed high expectations for the upcoming meeting in Shenzhen. He stressed that regional cooperation should go beyond expanding trade and attracting investment. It should also help smaller economies strengthen their technological and industrial capabilities, enabling them to benefit more fully from regional economic integration. China can play a constructive role in this process through technology sharing, skills development and improved market access. The APEC leaders' meeting, which will be held in Shenzhen, is expected to bring new momentum for regional economies to collaborate amid challenging times. By embracing openness and strengthening cooperation, Asia-Pacific economies can turn shared challenges into opportunities and work toward common prosperity. (Reporter: Li Wei, Video: Cheng Zixin)
